claim: Strongyloides stercoralis is estimated to infect ~600 million people worldwide.
source: It is estimated to infect ~600 million people worldwide and is endemic in Africa, Asia, Latin America, and parts of the Caribbean, southern United States and Europe (Buonfrate et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Buonfrate et al., 2020.

claim: S. stercoralis is endemic in Africa, Asia, Latin America, and parts of the Caribbean, southern United States and Europe.
source: It is estimated to infect ~600 million people worldwide and is endemic in Africa, Asia, Latin America, and parts of the Caribbean, southern United States and Europe (Buonfrate et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Buonfrate et al., 2020.

claim: Up to 2.5% of S. stercoralis infections will progress to a hyperinfection syndrome that has a 90% mortality rate if untreated.
source: Because of the unique nature of its lifecycle, S. stercoralis infections are often life-long and up to 2.5% of these infections will progress to a hyperinfection syndrome that has a 90% mortality rate if untreated (Milder et al., 1981).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Milder et al., 1981.

claim: S. stercoralis hyperinfections are often caused by administering glucocorticoids to otherwise asymptomatic patients.
source: Notably, such hyperinfections are often caused by administering glucocorticoids to otherwise asymptomatic patients (Milder et al., 1981).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Milder et al., 1981.

claim: Infective third-stage larvae (L3i) of S. stercoralis are developmentally quiescent and reside in fecal-contaminated soil until they contact the host and penetrate the skin.
source: Infective third-stage larvae (L3i) are developmentally quiescent and reside in fecal-contaminated soil until they contact the host and penetrate the skin, a process that reactivates their development as L3+ larvae.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: Skin penetration by L3i reactivates their development as L3+ larvae.
source: Infective third-stage larvae (L3i) are developmentally quiescent and reside in fecal-contaminated soil until they contact the host and penetrate the skin, a process that reactivates their development as L3+ larvae.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: In the host, activated L3+ larvae immediately begin feeding and typically migrate to the lungs, enter the alimentary canal, and transit to the intestine.
source: In the host, the activated L3+ immediately begin feeding, and typically migrate to the lungs, enter the alimentary canal, and transit to the intestine where the stage four larvae (L4) mature into parasitic (P)-adult females (there are no parasitic males).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: There are no parasitic males in S. stercoralis.
source: In the host, the activated L3+ immediately begin feeding, and typically migrate to the lungs, enter the alimentary canal, and transit to the intestine where the stage four larvae (L4) mature into parasitic (P)-adult females (there are no parasitic males).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: Parasitic adult females of S. stercoralis reproduce asexually.
source: The P-adult females reproduce asexually and generate rhabditiform, noninfectious stage one larvae (L1) progeny that can enter two alternate lifecycle routes, one in the external environment and one in the host.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: Under conditions that mimic the host intestine (e.g., 37°C), most PP-L1 develop as females directly into infectious filariform L3i.
source: Under conditions that mimic the host intestine (e.g., 37°C), most PP-L1 develop as females directly into infectious filariform L3i (Albarqi et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Albarqi et al., 2016.

claim: Under favorable conditions (e.g., 22 °C, high humidity) the majority of PP-L1 undergo a developmental switch and become free-living (FL) male and female larvae.
source: However, under favorable conditions (e.g., 22 °C, high humidity) the majority of PP-L1 undergo a developmental switch and become free-living (FL) male and female larvae that eventually mature into FL-adults, which are morphologically distinct from parasitic females and feed on soil microbes.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: Free-living adults of S. stercoralis are morphologically distinct from parasitic females and feed on soil microbes.
source: However, under favorable conditions (e.g., 22 °C, high humidity) the majority of PP-L1 undergo a developmental switch and become free-living (FL) male and female larvae that eventually mature into FL-adults, which are morphologically distinct from parasitic females and feed on soil microbes.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: Free-living adults mate and produce post-free-living (PFL) larvae that are exclusively female and definitively committed to become infective L3i larvae.
source: The FL-adults mate and produce post-free-living (PFL) larvae that are exclusively female and now definitively committed to become infective L3i larvae.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: S. stercoralis has the ability to remain in the host and undergo continuous autoinfection.
source: In addition to the conditions that produce L3i outside of the host, S. stercoralis has the ability to remain in the host and undergo continuous autoinfection (Figure 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Autoinfection in S. stercoralis is due to the presence of L1 larvae that develop directly into autoinfective third-stage larvae (L3a) within the intestine.
source: This is due to the presence of L1 larvae that develop directly into autoinfective third-stage larvae (L3a) within the intestine.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: L3a infect the host by penetrating the intestinal wall and entering parenteral tissues as activated L3+ to complete the parasitic lifecycle.
source: Similar to their L3i counterparts, L3a infect the host, in this case by penetrating the intestinal wall and entering parenteral tissues as activated L3+ to complete the parasitic lifecycle.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: Autoinfection is unique to S. stercoralis and allows the parasite to persist in the host for decades as a latent, often asymptomatic infection.
source: Autoinfection is unique to S. stercoralis and allows the parasite to persist in the host for decades as a latent, often asymptomatic infection.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: Under certain host conditions such as immunosuppression by glucocorticoids, autoinfection spirals out of control, dramatically increasing the parasite burden.
source: However, under certain host conditions such as immunosuppression by glucocorticoids, the autoinfection spirals out of control, dramatically increasing the parasite burden.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: Hyperinfection leads to a breakdown of the intestinal mucosal barrier and dissemination of invasive larvae throughout the body accompanied by bacterial infection leading to sepsis.
source: The resulting hyperinfection leads to a breakdown of the intestinal mucosal barrier and dissemination of invasive larvae throughout the body accompanied by bacterial infection leading to sepsis that is responsible for the high mortality.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: The current treatment of choice for strongyloidiasis is ivermectin.
source: The current treatment of choice is the nematode-selective chloride channel activator ivermectin, which is effective at controlling acute infections, but is limited by its inability to eradicate the persistent autoinfective larvae (Krolewiecki et al., 2013; Repetto et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Krolewiecki et al., 2013 and Repetto et al., 2018.

claim: Ivermectin is effective at controlling acute S. stercoralis infections, but is limited by its inability to eradicate the persistent autoinfective larvae.
source: The current treatment of choice is the nematode-selective chloride channel activator ivermectin, which is effective at controlling acute infections, but is limited by its inability to eradicate the persistent autoinfective larvae (Krolewiecki et al., 2013; Repetto et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Krolewiecki et al., 2013 and Repetto et al., 2018.

claim: The efficacy of ivermectin in preventing fatality due to hyperinfection and disseminated forms of strongyloidiasis is as low as 50%.
source: Perhaps for this reason, the efficacy of ivermectin in preventing fatality due to the hyperinfection and disseminated forms of the disease is as low as 50% (Buonfrate et al., 2013), and cases of ivermectin resistance are now being reported in other nematode parasites (Prichard, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Buonfrate et al., 2013.

claim: Cases of ivermectin resistance are now being reported in other nematode parasites.
source: Perhaps for this reason, the efficacy of ivermectin in preventing fatality due to the hyperinfection and disseminated forms of the disease is as low as 50% (Buonfrate et al., 2013), and cases of ivermectin resistance are now being reported in other nematode parasites (Prichard, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Prichard, 2007.

claim: The risk of hyperinfection has risen dramatically with the use of glucocorticoids to treat inflammatory diseases, particularly SARS-CoV-2.
source: Of further immediate concern, the risk of hyperinfection has risen dramatically with the use of glucocorticoids to treat inflammatory diseases, particularly SARS-CoV-2 (Moloo, 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Moloo, 2020.

claim: In C. elegans, L3d development is governed by DAF-12.
source: In C. elegans, L3d development is governed by DAF-12 (Antebi et al., 1998; Antebi et al., 2000), a nematode-specific nuclear receptor that is conserved in parasitic species (Ayoade et al., 2020; Long et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2019; Motola et al., 2006; Ogawa et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Antebi et al., 1998 and Antebi et al., 2000.

claim: DAF-12 is a nematode-specific nuclear receptor that is conserved in parasitic species.
source: In C. elegans, L3d development is governed by DAF-12 (Antebi et al., 1998; Antebi et al., 2000), a nematode-specific nuclear receptor that is conserved in parasitic species (Ayoade et al., 2020; Long et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2019; Motola et al., 2006; Ogawa et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations including Ayoade et al., 2020; Long et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2019; Motola et al., 2006; Ogawa et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2009.

claim: In favorable environments, developing C. elegans larvae synthesize the endogenous DAF-12 ligands called dafachronic acids.
source: In favorable environments, developing larvae synthesize the endogenous C. elegans (Ce)-DAF-12 ligands called dafachronic acids (Mahanti et al., 2014; Motola et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Mahanti et al., 2014 and Motola et al., 2006.

claim: Δ7-dafachronic acid (Δ7-DA) is the most potent and abundant endogenous DAF-12 ligand in C. elegans.
source: The most potent and abundant of these ligands is Δ7-dafachronic acid (Δ7-DA), which induces a transcriptional program that governs metabolism and reproductive growth to mature adults (Bethke et al., 2009; Hammell et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bethke et al., 2009; Hammell et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2015.

claim: Δ7-DA induces a transcriptional program that governs metabolism and reproductive growth to mature adults in C. elegans.
source: The most potent and abundant of these ligands is Δ7-dafachronic acid (Δ7-DA), which induces a transcriptional program that governs metabolism and reproductive growth to mature adults (Bethke et al., 2009; Hammell et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bethke et al., 2009; Hammell et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2015.

claim: The final and rate-limiting step of Δ7-DA synthesis is catalyzed by DAF-9, a cytochrome P450.
source: The final and rate-limiting step of Δ7-DA synthesis is catalyzed by DAF-9, a cytochrome P450 (Gerisch and Antebi, 2004; Jia et al., 2002; Motola et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gerisch and Antebi, 2004; Jia et al., 2002; Motola et al., 2006.

claim: In unfavorable environments, Δ7-DA is not produced and unliganded Ce-DAF-12 functions as a transcriptional repressor that arrests growth as L3d larvae in a process known as dauer diapause.
source: In unfavorable environments, Δ7-DA is not produced and unliganded Ce-DAF-12 functions as a transcriptional repressor that arrests growth as L3d larvae in a process known as dauer diapause.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: When favorable conditions return, Δ7-DA synthesis resumes, DAF-12 is transcriptionally active, and C. elegans worms exit L3 dauer and continue reproductive development.
source: When favorable conditions return, Δ7-DA synthesis resumes, DAF-12 is transcriptionally active, and worms exit L3 dauer and continue reproductive development.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: Pharmacologic administration of Δ7-DA to PP-L1 or PFL-L1 larvae commits them to FL reproductive development, even under conditions that would normally commit them to become L3i.
source: Although the endogenous Ss-DAF-12 ligand was unknown, we demonstrated that pharmacologic administration of Δ7-DA to PP-L1 or PFL-L1 larvae commits them to FL reproductive development, even under conditions that would normally commit them to become L3i (Albarqi et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2009), and institutes a transcriptomic profile in L3i similar to L3+ (Stoltzfus et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Albarqi et al., 2016 and Wang et al., 2009.

claim: Δ7-DA treatment institutes a transcriptomic profile in L3i similar to L3+.
source: Although the endogenous Ss-DAF-12 ligand was unknown, we demonstrated that pharmacologic administration of Δ7-DA to PP-L1 or PFL-L1 larvae commits them to FL reproductive development, even under conditions that would normally commit them to become L3i (Albarqi et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2009), and institutes a transcriptomic profile in L3i similar to L3+ (Stoltzfus et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stoltzfus et al., 2014.

claim: Knockout of Ss-DAF-12 prevents the formation of L3i larvae.
source: In addition, knockout of Ss-DAF-12 prevents the formation of L3i larvae (Cheong et al., 2021), and in a mouse model of hyperinfection, exogenous Δ7-DA treatment lowers the worm burden in the intestine (Patton et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cheong et al., 2021.

claim: In a mouse model of hyperinfection, exogenous Δ7-DA treatment lowers the worm burden in the intestine.
source: In addition, knockout of Ss-DAF-12 prevents the formation of L3i larvae (Cheong et al., 2021), and in a mouse model of hyperinfection, exogenous Δ7-DA treatment lowers the worm burden in the intestine (Patton et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Patton et al., 2018.

claim: Δ7-DA was the only ligand activity detected in fraction 23 of HPLC fractionation of S. stercoralis lipids.
source: Among the 70 high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) fractions, Ss-DAF-12 ligand activity was detected only in fraction 23 in a cell-based reporter assay and this activity was dose dependent (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Fraction 23 coeluted with dafachronic acids.
source: Remarkably, fraction 23 coeluted with dafachronic acids (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that the ligand is a related molecule.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The predicted endogenous concentration of Δ7-DA in S. stercoralis FL-L3 is ~200 nM.
source: The predicted endogenous concentration of Δ7-DA in S. stercoralis FL-L3 is ~200 nM, which is well above the concentration needed to fully activate Ss-DAF-12 (Figure 2B, inset).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The concentration of Δ7-DA in S. stercoralis FL-L3 (~200 nM) is well above the concentration needed to fully activate Ss-DAF-12.
source: The predicted endogenous concentration of Δ7-DA in S. stercoralis FL-L3 is ~200 nM, which is well above the concentration needed to fully activate Ss-DAF-12 (Figure 2B, inset).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2B inset.

claim: Δ7-DA was present in FL-L1/L2 and was significantly more abundant in the FL-L3 stage as the larvae progress toward reproductive maturity.
source: In the postparasitic environment under conditions that promote FL development, Δ7-DA was present in FL-L1/L2 and was significantly more abundant in the FL-L3 stage as the larvae progress toward reproductive maturity (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: Δ7-DA was detected in L3+ that have just infected the host and begun their reproductive development.
source: Similarly, Δ7-DA was detected in L3+ that have just infected the host and begun their reproductive development (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: Δ7-DA was undetectable in FL-adults, PFL-L1, and L3i larvae.
source: In concordance with the hypothesis that developmental arrest is due to the absence of a DAF-12 ligand, Δ7-DA was undetectable in FL-adults, PFL-L1, and L3i larvae (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: Intestinal (Int)-L1-L3a larvae that were the direct progeny of parasitic adults in hyperinfected gerbils had virtually no Δ7-DA.
source: The intestinal (Int)-L1-L3a larvae that were the direct progeny of parasitic adults in hyperinfected gerbils also had virtually no Δ7-DA (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: The highest concentration of Δ7-DA occurred in parasitic adults, as opposed to the essentially undetectable levels in FL adults.
source: Another intriguing finding was that the highest concentration of Δ7-DA occurred in parasitic adults, as opposed to the essentially undetectable levels in FL adults (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Parasitic adults live for up to a year or more in the host, whereas FL adults survive for only a few days in soil.
source: This difference in Δ7-DA levels correlated with the markedly different lifespans of the two adult populations. Parasitic adults live for up to a year or more in the host, whereas FL adults survive for only a few days in soil (Lok, 2007; Viney and Lok, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lok, 2007 and Viney and Lok, 2015.

claim: Δ7-DA is known to extend lifespan of adult C. elegans.
source: Given that Δ7-DA is known to extend lifespan of adult C. elegans (Gerisch et al., 2007; Yamawaki et al., 2010), this finding suggests that Δ7-DA may play a similar role in extending the lifespan of parasitic adults in S. stercoralis.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Gerisch et al., 2007 and Yamawaki et al., 2010.

claim: Δ7-DA may play a role in extending the lifespan of parasitic adults in S. stercoralis.
source: Given that Δ7-DA is known to extend lifespan of adult C. elegans (Gerisch et al., 2007; Yamawaki et al., 2010), this finding suggests that Δ7-DA may play a similar role in extending the lifespan of parasitic adults in S. stercoralis.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on inference from C. elegans data.

claim: The S. stercoralis genome contains single homologs for both DAF-36 and DHS-16.
source: Bioinformatic analysis of the S. stercoralis genome revealed single homologs for both DAF-36 and DHS-16 (Stoltzfus et al., 2012), which share sequence identity with their C. elegans counterparts.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stoltzfus et al., 2012.

claim: There are 26 CYPs in S. stercoralis, but none of these share predictive sequence identity with DAF-9 (~36% at the best).
source: In contrast, there are 26 CYPs in S. stercoralis, but none of these share predictive sequence identity with DAF-9 (~36% at the best) (Stoltzfus et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stoltzfus et al., 2012.

claim: S. stercoralis synthesizes Δ7-DA from dietary cholesterol in vivo.
source: After 24 hr, we detected significant levels of 13C-labeled Δ7-DA in the FL-L3 (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B demonstrating incorporation of 13C-cholesterol into Δ7-DA.

claim: Ss-DAF-36 catalyzes the synthesis of 7-dehydrocholesterol in the first step of Δ7-DA biosynthesis.
source: Sf9 microsomes expressing Ss-DAF-36 readily converted cholesterol to 7-dehydrocholesterol (Figure 4C) with an efficacy comparable to the C. elegans enzyme (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and 4D.

claim: Ss-SCDH-16 catalyzes the conversion of lathosterol to lathosterone in the penultimate step of Δ7-DA biosynthesis.
source: Similarly, Ss-SCDH-16 catalyzed the conversion of lathosterol to lathosterone like Ce-DHS-16 (Figure 4E, F).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E and 4F.

claim: Ss-CYP22a9 is the DAF-9 isoenzyme in S. stercoralis that synthesizes Δ7-DA from lathosterone.
source: Unambiguously, only one of the 26 CYPs, Ss-CYP22a9 (SSTP_0001032100) synthesized Δ7-DA at levels comparable to Ce-DAF-9 (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G demonstrating that only Ss-CYP22a9 among 26 CYPs tested synthesized Δ7-DA.

claim: In the presence of 8-Br-cGMP, endogenous Δ7-DA was increased progressively over a 3-day period to levels (~100 nM) that would saturate Ss-DAF-12 occupancy.
source: In the presence of 8-Br-cGMP, we found that endogenous Δ7-DA was increased progressively over a 3-day period to levels (~100 nM) that would saturate Ss-DAF-12 occupancy (Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Stimulation of Δ7-DA synthesis by 8-Br-cGMP correlated exactly with the expression of Ss-cyp22a9.
source: Furthermore, this stimulation of Δ7-DA synthesis correlated exactly with the expression of Ss-cyp22a9 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) and was abolished by cotreatment with ketoconazole, a broad-spectrum CYP inhibitor (Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Ketoconazole, a broad-spectrum CYP inhibitor, abolished the stimulation of Δ7-DA synthesis by 8-Br-cGMP.
source: Furthermore, this stimulation of Δ7-DA synthesis correlated exactly with the expression of Ss-cyp22a9 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) and was abolished by cotreatment with ketoconazole, a broad-spectrum CYP inhibitor (Figure 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Disruption of the Ss-cyp22a9 gene severely impaired cGMP-induced feeding behavior in L3i larvae.
source: In contrast, in Ss-cyp22a9 knockout larvae, cGMP-induced feeding behavior was severely impaired (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The loss of feeding behavior in Ss-cyp22a9-deficient larvae was rescued completely by treatment with exogenous Δ7-DA.
source: The loss of this feeding behavior in Ss-cyp22a9-deficient larvae was rescued completely by treatment with exogenous Δ7-DA, further demonstrating the importance of DAF-12 activation as a requirement for parasite development (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Disrupting the Ss-cyp22a9 gene abolished the Δ7-DA induction by cGMP.
source: Consistent with the results of the CYP inhibitor, disrupting the Ss-cyp22a9 gene abolished the Δ7-DA induction by cGMP (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Δ7-DA treatment for 14 days dramatically reduced fecal larval output by ~90% in gerbils with uncomplicated S. stercoralis infection.
source: Compared to vehicle, treatment with Δ7-DA for 14 days dramatically reduced fecal larval output by ~90% (312 ± 103 larvae per gram feces for vehicle vs 32 ± 6 for DA, q < 0.03; Figure 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The numbers of parasitic adults were not significantly changed by Δ7-DA treatment in gerbils with uncomplicated S. stercoralis infection.
source: In contrast, the numbers of parasitic adults, which produce intestinal larvae, were not significantly changed by Δ7-DA treatment (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: When hyperinfected gerbils were treated with Δ7-DA starting at 10 days after the hyperinfection was initiated, there was a 70% survival rate that lasted for at least 90 days.
source: In contrast, when a matched group of these animals was treated with Δ7-DA starting at 10 days after the hyperinfection was initiated, there was an impressive 70% survival rate that lasted for at least 90 days at which point we arbitrarily terminated the experiment (Figure 7A, blue line).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Hyperinfection resulted in a massive increase in the number of viable intestinal parasites (>104) in vehicle-treated gerbils, which was reduced substantially in Δ7-DA-treated animals.
source: Autopsies of these animals showed that hyperinfection resulted in a massive increase in the number of viable intestinal parasites (>104) in vehicle-treated gerbils, which was reduced substantially in Δ7-DA-treated animals (Figure 7A-D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A-D.

claim: The number of autoinfected L3+ larvae in parenteral tissues was reduced by 90% (and in some cases was undetectable) in Δ7-DA-treated animals compared to vehicle-treated animals.
source: Notably, the number of autoinfected L3+ larvae in parenteral tissues, which drive the resulting pathogenesis, was reduced by 90% (and in some cases was undetectable) in Δ7-DA-treated animals compared to vehicle-treated animals (Figure 7C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: There was a >10-fold increase in adult parasites in hyperinfected vehicle-treated gerbils compared to vehicle-treated gerbils with uncomplicated infections.
source: Compared to vehicle-treated gerbils with uncomplicated infections (Figure 6B), we observed a >10-fold increase in adult parasites in hyperinfected vehicle-treated gerbils (Figure 7D).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of experimental data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 7D.

claim: There was a significant decrease in adult parasites in the Δ7-DA-treated gerbils that had a hyperinfection (50% vs. the vehicle treated).
source: However, unlike in the uncomplicated infection, there was a significant decrease in adult parasites in the Δ7-DA-treated gerbils that had a hyperinfection (50% vs. the vehicle treated, Figure 7D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Ivermectin treatment at 300 μg/kg delivered i.p. acutely cleared fecal larva output in ~40% of the hyperinfected gerbils within 7 days, resulting in ~25% survival rate for at least 90 days.
source: In this model, 300 μg/kg ivermectin delivered i.p. acutely cleared fecal larva output in ~40% of the hyperinfected gerbils within 7 days, resulting in ~25% survival rate for at least 90 days (Figure 7A, red line).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Ivermectin was as effective as Δ7-DA in removing adult parasites from animals undergoing hyperinfection.
source: As expected, ivermectin was as effective as Δ7-DA in removing adult parasites from animals undergoing hyperinfection (Figure 7D), but in contrast to Δ7-DA, ivermectin was ineffective at decreasing either the intestinal or L3+ larval populations (Figure 7B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Ivermectin was ineffective at decreasing either the intestinal or L3+ larval populations in hyperinfected gerbils.
source: As expected, ivermectin was as effective as Δ7-DA in removing adult parasites from animals undergoing hyperinfection (Figure 7D), but in contrast to Δ7-DA, ivermectin was ineffective at decreasing either the intestinal or L3+ larval populations (Figure 7B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B and 7C.

claim: The combination of Δ7-DA and ivermectin improved the survival rate significantly over either agent alone (>75%) in hyperinfected gerbils.
source: We found that the combination of both agents improved the survival rate significantly over either agent alone (>75%, Figure 7A) and reduced the parasite burden of all life stages (Figure 7B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The combination of Δ7-DA and ivermectin reduced the parasite burden of all life stages in hyperinfected gerbils.
source: We found that the combination of both agents improved the survival rate significantly over either agent alone (>75%, Figure 7A) and reduced the parasite burden of all life stages (Figure 7B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B-D.

claim: The combination of Δ7-DA and ivermectin completely eliminated the parasites from all the animals that survived hyperinfection.
source: Remarkably, the combination of Δ7-DA and ivermectin completely eliminated the parasites from all the animals that survived, essentially curing them of the disease (Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: When treated with ivermectin or Δ7-DA alone, ≤10% of surviving animals were parasite-free.
source: In contrast, when treated with ivermectin or Δ7-DA alone, ≤10% were parasite-free even among those animals that survived (Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Mortality rates in ivermectin-treated patients with hyperinfection range as high as 50%.
source: Mortality rates in ivermectin-treated patients with hyperinfection range as high as 50% (Buonfrate et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Buonfrate et al., 2013.

claim: Ivermectin is highly effective at killing adults and feeding larvae but less effective at killing the developmentally quiescent L3a larvae.
source: As an inhibitor of muscular function, ivermectin is highly effective at killing adults and feeding larvae (Repetto et al., 2018), but less effective at killing the developmentally quiescent L3a larvae that continuously drive autoinfection.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Repetto et al., 2018 and by inference from the mechanism of action.

claim: Δ7-DA directly interferes with infectious L3a larval development by binding to unliganded DAF-12 and provoking an inappropriate developmental response inside the host that results in death of the larvae.
source: In contrast, Δ7-DA directly interferes with infectious L3a larval development by binding to unliganded DAF-12 and provoking an inappropriate developmental response inside the host that results in death of the larvae.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data and the known mechanism of DAF-12 activation.

claim: The ligand binding pocket of Ss-DAF-12 is divergent from that of Ce-DAF-12.
source: Indeed, the finding that the ligand binding pocket of Ss-DAF-12 is divergent from that of Ce-DAF-12 (Wang et al., 2009) and the observation that S. stercoralis lacks an obvious ortholog of DAF-9 (the only known DA-synthesizing enzyme found in C. elegans) suggested that the Ss-DAF-12 ligand would likewise be divergent.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2009.

claim: The Ss-DAF-12 ligand binding domain shares only moderate sequence identity (42%) with its C. elegans homolog.
source: In comparison to its C. elegans homolog, the Ss-DAF-12 ligand binding domain shares only moderate sequence identity (42%) and exhibits a distinct pharmacologic profile in response to Δ7-DA compared to other species (Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2009.

claim: Ss-DAF-12 exhibits a distinct pharmacologic profile in response to Δ7-DA compared to other species.
source: In comparison to its C. elegans homolog, the Ss-DAF-12 ligand binding domain shares only moderate sequence identity (42%) and exhibits a distinct pharmacologic profile in response to Δ7-DA compared to other species (Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2009.

claim: The cytochrome P450 (Ss-CYP22a9) that catalyzes the synthesis of Δ7-DA is unique to Strongyloides spp.
source: For example, the cytochrome P450 (Ss-CYP22a9) that catalyzes the synthesis of Δ7-DA (Figure 4) and the ligand-dependent coactivator that Ss-DAF-12 requires for transactivation (Ss-DIP-1) (Cheong et al., 2021) are both unique to Strongyloides spp.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: The ligand-dependent coactivator that Ss-DAF-12 requires for transactivation (Ss-DIP-1) is unique to Strongyloides spp.
source: For example, the cytochrome P450 (Ss-CYP22a9) that catalyzes the synthesis of Δ7-DA (Figure 4) and the ligand-dependent coactivator that Ss-DAF-12 requires for transactivation (Ss-DIP-1) (Cheong et al., 2021) are both unique to Strongyloides spp.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cheong et al., 2021.

claim: No other ligand activities, including other types of dafachronic acids, were detected in S. stercoralis.
source: First, no other ligand activities, including other types of dafachronic acids were detected.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental data from the ligand purification and detection studies.

claim: Knocking out Ss-cyp22a9 prevents DAF-12-dependent activity in vivo, and that activity is rescued completely by adding back the ligand.
source: Finally, knocking out the daf-9 homolog, Ss-cyp22a9, which is required to synthesize Δ7-DA, prevents DAF-12-dependent activity in vivo, and that activity is rescued completely by adding back the ligand.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Δ7-DA has been shown to activate DAF-12 homologs in other species.
source: Interestingly, Δ7-DA has been shown to activate DAF-12 homologs in other species (Ayoade et al., 2020; Long et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2019; Ogawa et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations including Ayoade et al., 2020; Long et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2019; Ogawa et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2009.

claim: Liganded DAF-12 is required at a completely different but essential stage of the lifecycle to promote reproductive growth.
source: However, the observation that liganded DAF-12 also is required at a completely different but essential stage of the lifecycle to promote reproductive growth raises the possibility of also targeting DAF-12 with an antagonist.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental data showing Δ7-DA levels correlate with reproductive development.

claim: DAF-12 has been found in all nematode species surveyed to date.
source: Given that DAF-12 has been found in all nematode species surveyed to date (Ayoade et al., 2020; Long et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2019; Ogawa et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2009), antagonizing the receptor would be expected to prevent development of adult worms in all parasitic species, offering a unique, broad-spectrum approach for treating most, if not all, nematode parasitisms.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations including Ayoade et al., 2020; Long et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2019; Ogawa et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2009.

claim: Antagonizing DAF-12 would be expected to prevent development of adult worms in all parasitic species.
source: Given that DAF-12 has been found in all nematode species surveyed to date (Ayoade et al., 2020; Long et al., 2020; Ma et al., 2019; Ogawa et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2009), antagonizing the receptor would be expected to prevent development of adult worms in all parasitic species, offering a unique, broad-spectrum approach for treating most, if not all, nematode parasitisms.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on inference from the conservation of DAF-12 across nematode species.

claim: Ketoconazole was shown previously to block developmental activation of cultured L3i.
source: Indeed, the finding that the broad-spectrum CYP-inhibitor, ketoconazole, was effective at blocking Δ7-DA synthesis in the present study and was shown previously to block developmental activation of cultured L3i (Albarqi et al., 2016) supports this strategy.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Albarqi et al., 2016.

claim: Δ7-DA has a short half-life and relatively poor pharmacokinetic properties in vivo.
source: Typical of most endogenous steroid receptor ligands, Δ7-DA has a short half-life and relatively poor pharmacokinetic properties in vivo (Patton et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Patton et al., 2018.

claim: Pharmacological activation of Ss-DAF-12 overcomes the deficiencies of ivermectin and significantly improves the outcome of strongyloidiasis in a preclinical model of hyperinfection.
source: Our study further revealed the ligand's biosynthetic enzyme as a potential new target that might also be exploited to treat this lethal parasitic disease.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Pharmacologically activating DAF-12 prevents L3i arrest in the PFL generation.
source: Pharmacologically activating the nuclear receptor DAF-12 has been shown to prevent L3i arrest in the PFL generation (Albarqi et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Albarqi et al., 2016 and Wang et al., 2009, and is illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: Liganded DAF-12 in S. stercoralis is required for reproductive development.
source: Taken together with our previous work demonstrating that parasites lacking Ss-DAF-12 fail to respond to Δ7-DA and cannot enter or exit the L3i stage (Cheong et al., 2021), we conclude that liganded DAF-12 in S. stercoralis is required for reproductive development, while unliganded DAF-12 is requisite for the production of infectious L3i and L3a larvae.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data and previous work cited (Cheong et al., 2021).

claim: Unliganded DAF-12 is requisite for the production of infectious L3i and L3a larvae in S. stercoralis.
source: Taken together with our previous work demonstrating that parasites lacking Ss-DAF-12 fail to respond to Δ7-DA and cannot enter or exit the L3i stage (Cheong et al., 2021), we conclude that liganded DAF-12 in S. stercoralis is required for reproductive development, while unliganded DAF-12 is requisite for the production of infectious L3i and L3a larvae.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data and previous work cited (Cheong et al., 2021).

claim: Δ7-DA synthesis is necessary for parasite reproduction in S. stercoralis.
source: Genetic loss of function of the ligand's rate-limiting enzyme demonstrated that Δ7-DA synthesis is necessary for parasite reproduction, whereas its absence is required for the development of infectious larvae.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The absence of Δ7-DA is required for the development of infectious larvae in S. stercoralis.
source: Genetic loss of function of the ligand's rate-limiting enzyme demonstrated that Δ7-DA synthesis is necessary for parasite reproduction, whereas its absence is required for the development of infectious larvae.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Availability of the Δ7-DA ligand permits Ss-DAF-12 to function as an on/off switch governing autoinfection.
source: Availability of the ligand permits Ss-DAF-12 to function as an on/off switch governing autoinfection, making it vulnerable to therapeutic intervention.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing Δ7-DA levels correlate with developmental stages.

claim: In a preclinical model of hyperinfection, pharmacologic activation of DAF-12 suppressed autoinfection and markedly reduced lethality.
source: In a preclinical model of hyperinfection, pharmacologic activation of DAF-12 suppressed autoinfection and markedly reduced lethality.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: When Δ7-DA was administered with ivermectin, the combinatorial effects of the two drugs resulted in a near cure of strongyloidiasis.
source: Moreover, when Δ7-DA was administered with ivermectin, the current but limited drug of choice for treating strongyloidiasis, the combinatorial effects of the two drugs resulted in a near cure of the disease.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 7.
